blocker_detail: The skill's entire mechanism is: the controller session dispatches independent, context-isolated subagents (one implementer per task, one reviewer per task, a final whole-branch reviewer) and coordinates them via a ledger/workspace. This requires an in-process subagent-spawning tool (e.g. a 'Task' tool that launches a fresh Claude agent with its own isolated context and returns a report). This runtime's tool list has no such tool: no Task/dispatch tool, and no ListAgents to discover/target one. The only capability in the toolset that creates a new independent agent is mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_session, which is an explicit session-management tool that the task's safety rules forbid calling. SendMessage exists but only routes to already-existing agents found via ListAgents (also unavailable), so it cannot originate a fresh subagent either. I set up the plan file, a git repo, and the ledger/workspace convention the skill describes (all of which worked fine), but could not perform the one operation that defines the skill: actually dispatching an isolated subagent to implement Task 1 and a separate one to review it. I did the implementation and review myself in the same context as a workaround, which is precisely the 'controller fixes/does the work' anti-pattern the skill explicitly forbids, so it does not count as achieving the skill's deliverable.
